questionText: The product of all eigenvalues of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$ is
explanation:
Step 1: Recall the property of eigenvalues
The product of all eigenvalues of a matrix $A$ is equal to the determinant of $A$, i.e., $\prod \lambda_i = \det(A)$.

Step 2: Calculate the determinant of the matrix
Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$.

We can expand $\det(A)$ along the first row:
$\det(A) = 1 \cdot (5 \cdot 9 - 6 \cdot 8) - 2 \cdot (4 \cdot 9 - 6 \cdot 7) + 3 \cdot (4 \cdot 8 - 5 \cdot 7)$
$\det(A) = 1 \cdot (45 - 48) - 2 \cdot (36 - 42) + 3 \cdot (32 - 35)$
$\det(A) = 1 \cdot (-3) - 2 \cdot (-6) + 3 \cdot (-3)$
$\det(A) = -3 + 12 - 9 = 0$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $0$, the product of all eigenvalues is $0$.

Thus, the correct option is (B).
